findings.issue: A16's frozen catalogue contradicts A37's refund approval design, and A37 records no A16 loop for it. A16 row 84 binds order.refund (batch) to action code 'order.refund.batch' (singular) with policy 4E only. A37 raises 'orders.refund.batch' and lets it resolve to AUTO, but A16 checks the action code and 'the policy A14 resolved at submit'. A16 row 85 also keeps a separate order.refund (revert) row bound to offering:<id> under the offer.revert_and_refund approval, and says 'A37 passes the revert approval id'. A37 forbids that id (ORD_REFUND_APPROVAL_REQUIRED), and its negative challenge expects A16 to refuse it with LDG_APPROVAL_MISMATCH. Built as written, every refund journal fails A16's binding, and the 37-order failed-raise challenge and its negative case cannot both pass against the real A16. A37's loop A38.1 item 2 also says A71 already uses orders.refund.batch; A71 says A37 spells it order.refund.batch.
findings.fix: Record loop A16.2 with A16's owner: rename the batch row's code to orders.refund.batch; let that row accept A14's 4E row and its AUTO row (file_sha256_equals_approved against an approved offer.revert_and_refund); delete the separate revert row (or state it is never used for journals); remove 'A37 passes the revert approval id'. Add A16.2 to the Specify list of loops that must be agreed before the build, and correct the A71 wording in loop A38.1 item 2.

findings.issue: A03 section 2.7's actor rules for SM-05 are not covered by loop A03.1. Only submitted->cancelled and reflection_period->revoked are 'self'; every other transition is SVCA only. As a result: (1) the revocation hook and the placement replay run submitted->cancelled and reflection_period->revoked as a system actor, which A03 refuses; (2) the new awaiting_funds->cancelled edge has no actor list, so it defaults to SVCA and the investor's own cancel is refused; (3) funded->refund_pending on an investor cancel has no investor actor; (4) whether an AGNT principal counts as 'self' is not stated. Also, sending unfunded orders to 'expired' at a material-change deadline breaks A03's funds_not_received guard (now >= fundsDueAt) whenever reconfirm_due_at comes before funding_deadline_at. The 'Guards on' challenge will fail, or the builder will bypass the runner.
findings.fix: Extend loop A03.1 with actor rows. submitted->cancelled: self, AGNT on behalf of self, or SVCA with reason agent_*. reflection_period->revoked: self, AGNT, or SVCA on revocation. awaiting_funds->cancelled: self, AGNT, or SVCA on revocation. funded->refund_pending: self or AGNT (investor_cancelled) and SVCA (the rest). Either widen funds_not_received with a reconfirm_lapsed condition, or route those orders to cancelled with a new reason. Add every one of these to the 'Guards on' challenge with actor checks on.

findings.issue: The G07 rule at allocation contradicts itself. Step 1 excludes and fully refunds any investor-level 'fail' in A19's order_allocation set, and that set includes G07. A19's G07 evaluator fails when holdings + open orders + requested exceed the cap (A19's own challenge expects the second order to 'fail there'). Steps 2 and 4 instead cap the line to max_allowed_units. So an over-cap holder is either excluded entirely or capped, depending on which paragraph the builder follows. The 'Holder cap through the back door' challenge cannot happen as written: the second 300-unit order exceeds the quoted maximum of 100, so G07 rejects it at placement, and it never reaches allocation to be capped to 400.
findings.fix: State that at allocation a G07 fail is not an exclusion reason: its max_allowed_units feeds step 2's allowance and the line is capped with capped_at_holder_cap. Record in loop A19.1 that A19's order_allocation G07 returns the allowance for capping, not a stopping fail. Rewrite the challenge so the pair is valid at placement (for example, the associate's 100 units land on the register after both orders are funded), then capped to 400 at allocation.

findings.issue: Pro-rata with holder capping is not specified precisely enough for a byte-for-byte oracle. Steps 3 and 4 'repeat over the uncapped lines', but the note never defines the pool for a later round, which quantity is scaled (requested or remaining), whether largest-remainder distribution runs again in each round, or whether first_come applies the cap before or after the fill. Fable's hidden oracle and the builder can each pick a different, defensible reading.
findings.fix: Write the algorithm as numbered pseudocode: allowance_i = min(requested_i, cap_i); pool = hard_cap; loop: for uncapped lines, share_i = floor(req_i x pool / sum req_uncapped), then largest remainder, then funded_at, then id; lines with share > allowance are fixed at allowance, pool -= allowance, and the loop repeats. For first_come, fill in funded_at order with min(requested, allowance, remaining). Add two worked vectors with expected lines.

findings.issue: One design figure A37 pins as fixture truth is arithmetically wrong. SPN-07's row 'Ridgeline Pty Ltd, 460, A$110,208.32' should be 460 x A$238.40 = A$109,664.00 plus a 0.5% fee of A$548.32, which is A$110,212.32. The other four rows are correct. The design-fidelity challenge demands 'field for field' agreement, while the fee oracle demands mulBp, so one must fail, or the builder hard-codes the design number.
findings.fix: Record this as a design defect (for A51/A63 and design-analysis). The contract returns 11021232 cents for Ridgeline, and the fidelity test skips that cell with a named exception.

findings.issue: The state -> status_label map is 'a fixed map in the module' but is never written down, and the vocabulary (in_escrow, allotted, scaled_back, settled, ...) conflicts with A03 section 2.6, where 'Allotted' (grey) is SM-05 settled and 'In escrow' is funded. Fable cannot write the contract test from the spec, and A57 and A71 may draw different labels for allocated versus settled.
findings.fix: Tabulate the map for every state and refund_state combination, aligned with A03 section 2.6, with the design tone for each, and make it the contract test input.

findings.issue: Replaying an agent order confirmed after a 428 makes 'the person' the acknowledging actor, 'the person opens and acknowledges the documents in A60's confirmation step through A35'. A60's confirmation card has no document-open or acknowledgement step, and A12's confirm needs only a passkey over the payload hash. On a per-action-cap 428 (disclosure covered by standing consent), the replay would reach recordAcknowledgements with a person who opened nothing. The order would be rejected under G12, and the challenge 'person confirms -> exactly one funded order' fails.
findings.fix: Choose one rule. Either the replay records acknowledgements with the token actor (the delegated path, which the consent already covers) plus the person's passkey confirmation, and uses the person path only when the 428 was ACK_PERSON_REQUIRED. Or record loop A60 to add the documents_required open-and-acknowledge step to the confirmation card. Add a vector for each 428 kind.

findings.issue: A19's G11 evaluator at order_allocation would hold every oversubscribed pro-rata offering. Its rule is 'raised + pending + requested <= hard_cap, or may_be_scaled_back'. At allocation the funded total exceeds the hard cap, so orders without the flag fail. A37 treats a G11 failure as offering-level ORD_ALLOCATION_HELD, so the lock can never be requested. Loop A19.1 changes only the placement ceiling.
findings.fix: Add to loop A19.1: at order_allocation, G11 passes when the offering is closed with its soft cap reached and the funded total <= acceptance_ceiling_units, because scale-back is the allocation's job. Add a pro-rata challenge funded to 11,500 on a 10,000 hard cap in which the lock proceeds.

findings.issue: The returned-deposit path does not say which order a payment.reversal_pending affects. Credits pool in investor_cash and fund orders oldest-first, so a returned bank transaction may map to no order, one order or several, or only partly to one. The note also never says when A37 calls A17's completePendingReversal. The failed-raise challenge speaks of an order 'partially reversed', which the spec never defines.
findings.fix: Define the rule: cover the reversal from available investor_cash first; for the shortfall, move the most recently funded open orders to refund_pending (deposit_returned) until it is covered. After the refund journal posts, call completePendingReversal(bank_txn_id). Replace 'partially reversed' in the challenge with a defined case.

findings.issue: The escrow-release interface is still unresolved across notes. A37's frozen table names A39 as the caller of getEscrowReleaseBasis and of the refund-batch reads, and loop A39.1 asks the graph to add A37 to A39's deps. A39's current text says the opposite: 'A39 does not call A37, which is not an ancestor: the release basis is this event plus A16's offer_escrow sub-balances'. A39 also speaks of a fee share 'A37 may draw from fee_payable_realx', which A37 says it never does. So getEscrowReleaseBasis has no real caller, and nothing ensures that scale_back refund lines are handled before release.
findings.fix: Pick one design with A39's owner. Either A39 calls getEscrowReleaseBasis (add the A37 -> A39 edge in the graph and correct A39's line), or drop A39 from the callers column and state the release precondition A39 must check itself. Also correct A39's fee_payable_realx sentence to point to loop A16.1.

findings.issue: The pro-rata money challenge cannot be set up with the default parameters. Twelve orders totalling 12,000 units on a 10,000-unit offering average 1,000 units each, above the default 5% holder cap of 500 units, so G07 rejects most of them at placement. The spec gives no holder_cap_bps or investor mix for the vector.
findings.fix: Give the vector's parameters: holder_cap_bps (for example 1,500), twelve distinct unassociated investors, and the exact requested sizes.

findings.issue: Investor-facing contracts could tip off an AML exclusion. exclusion_gate (for example G14 or G02) and the excluded_at_allocation flag are fields on the order, and the spec does not say whether me/orders/{id} or the SPN-07 rows expose the gate code.
findings.fix: State that exclusion_gate is staff-only. Investor and sponsor contracts show a neutral status, for example 'Not allocated · refunded in full', with no gate code for G02, G14 or a freeze. Assert this in the G02 challenge.
